lead.headline: 74-90 California doctor-shortage areas holding 2.7-3.5M people are up for removal with no replacement, about 3x the national rate
lead.number: Builder: 123 of 214 active California shortage areas (57%) proposed for withdrawal, 4.62M people; after removing areas already re-designated under new IDs, 74-90 areas and 2.7-3.5M people remain.
lead.watch_out: 4.62M counts people already re-designated under new IDs (1.06M of the 2.91M "still designated" sit on the same tracts); 85% of the July 2026 withdrawals are old IDs retired after re-designation.

sources.page_context: al Federal Register notice (FRN) not later than July 1 of each year listing designated HPSAs. This FRN serves as notice that HPSAs that were placed in a proposed for withdrawal status due to state primary care office (PCO) actions between October 16, 2024, and September 21, 2025, will be withdrawn. HPSAs that did not pass the National Shortage Designation Update conducted in September 2025 will be maintained in a proposed for withdrawal status after the publication of this FRN, and the state PCOs will be allowed additional time to review and update designations. HRSA intends to address those HPSAs with the publication of the FRN on or before July 1, 2027.
